title: fix(app-shell): the AI drawer's conversation follows the app
body:

_Requested by **Yibo Wang** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01BVUyyPie8gHwoPM18iABwB?thread=cmsg_01BVUyyPie8gHwoPM18iABwBLW6dHPW6sSheA32XPKZzPV)_
Fixes #35014
Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none
Tier: not governed (`check-governed-merges --branch` on the final file list: 0 of 7 paths hit the register; 353 changed lines, under 3000)

## 维护者速读

- **改了什么**：控制台 AI 助手抽屉的对话现在跟着应用走。在应用 A 里打开过的对话，切到应用 B 后不再显示，B 显示自己的对话或空白开始页；回到 A，A 的那一段（含未发布的方案）还在。首页和平台自带应用仍用不绑定应用的那一段。问数（ask）不按应用分。
- **为什么改**：抽屉一旦指向过某段对话，就一直显示它，而范围已经写成新应用，在 B 里发的话可能改到 A。维护者裁定：不提示，自动切换。
- **风险与回滚**：只改前端抽屉的取值逻辑（每段对话记下打开时所在的应用），不改服务端存储。回滚即还原本 PR。卡上第 4 条（历史列表默认只列当前应用、「全部」开关）没有做：对话列表的每一行不带应用信息，需要服务端先记下对话所属应用，因依赖 cloud 端改动，席位已转交 triage 另立卡片（#32588）；卡上其余五条都在本 PR 完成。
- **先看**：`ui/packages/app-shell/src/layout/useConsoleChatDock.tsx`（`shownTarget` 那一行决定抽屉显示什么）；`ui/packages/app-shell/src/layout/chatDockTarget.ts`（`dockTargetFollowsApp` 的判定）；`ChatDock.appBinding-10926.test.tsx` 新增的 describe。
- **两分钟验证**：`cd ui && pnpm exec vitest run packages/app-shell/src/layout/__tests__/ChatDock.appBinding-10926.test.tsx`，预期 19 个用例全绿；或在应用 A 里用 AI 搭建后切到应用 B 打开抽屉，看到的是 B 的空白开始页、范围写 B。
- **需要你做的**：无，席位落地。

## What changes

The console's AI drawer kept showing a thread after the user moved to another app. Once the drawer had been pointed at a thread (a history row, "New chat", the app switcher, "Edit with AI"), the drawer body preferred `target.packageId` over the app in view, so the scope chip named app B while the content was app A's thread.

- `chatDockTarget.ts`: a target now records the app it was opened in (`app`: the authorable package in view, or `null` outside any app). `placeDockTarget` stamps it; `dockTargetFollowsApp` answers whether the drawer shows it in the app in view: yes in the app it was opened in, and in the app it names; anywhere else no. `ambientAppPackage` is the one resolver for "the app a build thread binds to" (the ui ADR-0057 Amendment A2 predicate), now shared by the host and the body.
- `useConsoleChatDock.tsx`: the host stamps every target it is given with the app in view (read through a ref kept in a layout effect, so a child effect that binds a package in the same commit reads the right app) and hands the body only a target that follows the app. The target stays stored per tab, so coming back to the app shows it again. A target stored before it had an `app` (an old `/ai…` link the redirect stored) is placed in the first app it is read in.
- `ChatDockConversation.tsx`: unchanged logic; it now reads the shared resolver, and a comment states that a target reaches it only in its own app.
- Card item by item:
  1. Entering another app resolves that app's scope: its latest thread, or the blank start page. The previous app's target is not carried over. Pinned.
  2. One thread, one app: the header chip names the thread's app. Picking another app in the scope switcher switches to that app's thread and never re-binds the current one. Pinned (a preservation pin: the switcher already did this on main).
  3. Home and the built-in apps keep the unbound thread. Pinned.
  4. **Not in this PR.** See Acceptance notes.
  5. The unpublished plan stays in its app's thread: back in A, A's thread is shown again on `app:PKG:build`, the key the Studio copilot reads. Pinned.
  6. `ask` is not split per app. ui ADR-0057 Amendment A2 says "`ask` stays ambient", and root ADR-0063 makes `ask` the RLS-bounded data product over the user's records, not an app-authoring thread, so there is no app for it to bind to. Pinned: the ask thread is the same in every app and no `app:PKG:ask` key is written.
- The Studio copilot and the drawer in the same app still share one thread (same `app:PKG:build` key; existing pins stay green).

- Red on main: the three source files restored from `origin/main` 357fb1ea45 (blob-checked), the new pins run: 5 failed, 14 passed (the 5 are the follow-the-app pins; the switcher and ask pins pass on main by design). Restored after; `git diff HEAD` empty.

## Acceptance notes

- **Card item 4 went to triage because of the cloud dependency (seat 3 ruling, filed on #32588); the card's other five items are delivered here.** The history list cannot default to the current app's threads from what the client has: a row of `GET /ai/conversations` carries no app (`ConversationListItem` is id, title, agent, timestamps, preview), and the create sends `{}`, so only the browser that keyed a thread knows its scope. The client can derive an app only for a thread whose own history drafted a package, or for the latest thread per app cached in this browser; any other thread (another device, an ask-style turn, a build that has not drafted yet) has no app the client can read, so a "current app only" default would hide some of the app's own threads. A complete filter needs the server to record each conversation's app; the card rules that out of this PR. The seat took route A: a cloud card for service-ai to record and return each conversation's app, then an objectstack follow-up blocked by it.
- A thread picked from the history keeps the behaviour from before this PR: it opens in the app the user is in, and the chip names the thread's own bound app when its history has one. The card's "navigate to that app first" belongs to item 4 and needs the same per-row app.
- A thread picked through the scope switcher for app B while in app A is shown in A, and in B. It is shown again in A after a visit elsewhere, because it is the last thing opened in A. The header and the content agree in both places.
- An agent-only target (picking Ask in app A) is stamped with A as well: in app B the drawer shows B's own thread, and the ask thread is unchanged and one tap away.

## Verification

- Local gates: the `dispatch-gates.mjs --commands` list for this diff, all exit 0 (the full list at fb542eb214; at 392ce0e92e the list was re-derived, came out the same, and its fast part was run again). `overlap-check.mjs`: clean against origin/main 357fb1ea45, 0 open PR heads share a file.
